channel.title: Eastern Daily Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Eastern Daily Press (edp24.co.uk)

item.title: Norwich delivery drivers to be deported after immigration crackdown
item.description: Indian delivery drivers working illegally in the UK are to be deported after being arrested while working in Norwich as part of a crackdown by the Home Office.

item.title: Go-ahead for new village homes despite 'overcrowding' fears
item.description: Five new homes have been given the go-ahead in Terrington St Clement despite a slew of objections.

item.title: Zoo faces six-figure business rates bill after being hit by budget hikes
item.description: Banham Zoo faces a six-figure business rates bill of more than £106,000 a year - up 65pc - following the chancellor Rachel Reeves' budget.

item.title: City's new pigeon scarer calls for people to stop feeding birds at the market
item.description: Adrian Diamond from NBC Environment, has been appointed by City Hall to scare away the pigeons at the top of the market using his falcon Travis.

item.title: Dog training college enters liquidation... but mystery buyer may have purchased brand
item.description: Innovaze Ltd, the company that runs Dog Training College, has entered liquidation after losing more than £180,000 last year.

item.title: Historic whalers' tavern and listed buildings damaged during regeneration work
item.description: Owners of historic buildings in King's Lynn's ancient whaling quarter are at loggerheads with Freebridge Community Housing over damage they say was caused by lorries serving a major regeneration project.

item.title: Meet the winner of this year's Granny of the Year competition
item.description: This year’s Granny of the Year feature showcased the remarkable spirit, kindness, and resilience of so many extraordinary women. Each nominee brought her own story of devotion, humour, and inspiration, making the editor’s decision an especially difficult one.

item.title: Farmers and landowners warned of criminals dumping lorry loads of illegal waste
item.description: Farmers and landowners across East Anglia have been warned to guard against criminals dumping lorry loads of illegal waste on rural land this winter.

item.title: New housing development in Norfolk's 'bottleneck' village gets go-ahead
item.description: Planners have given the go-ahead for 25 new houses in Coltishall.

item.title: Protestors' defiant message to council that wants to tear down bus shelter
item.description: A group of protestors stand defiant as they fight to save their beloved bus shelter in Sheringham from being torn down by Norfolk County Council.
